title: Cerebral palsy, hereditary ataxia, Huntington's and anoxic brain damage
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's neurological condition (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for cognitive status and memory deficits.

HPI
The patient is a 65-year-old woman who presents today for a scheduled follow-up regarding her neurological status. She has a history of anoxic brain damage resulting from a cardiac arrest that occurred two years ago. She continues to experience significant memory and attention deficits as a result of this anoxic brain injury. She resides at home and relies on her family for daily support and supervision. She reports that her memory remains inconsistent, but she is stable in her current environment.

Medication List
None reported at this time.

Exam
The patient is alert and cooperative. She is oriented to person but has difficulty with recent events. Her speech is clear. Motor strength is 5/5 throughout. Her attention span is limited, consistent with her history.

Assessment
1. Anoxic brain damage following cardiac arrest.
2. Memory and attention deficits.

Plan
Continue current management with family support. We will monitor her cognitive status and safety at home. Follow up in six months for a repeat evaluation.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD, 05/14/2026

distractors.why: The lasting brain damage is a current condition: G93.1.
